findings.explanation: R0945 was ranked 3rd on lexical hits for 'batch', 'cost', 'per', 'total', 'serbian' but every registered content item concerns cost-of-quality (PAF/appraisal-failure) modelling and inspection policy in electronics contract manufacturing (E191, E108, E059, E063, E045, E034, E117, E014, E148, E112). Nothing in the evidence covers bioinformatics pipelines, short-read alignment, variant/star-allele calling, Snakemake, Python workflow optimisation, or cloud instance cost engineering. His open_to (E052) is explicitly scoped to electronics manufacturers and CoQ/PAF consulting, and his notes (E120) demand 12+ months of defect/rework records plus limited capacity before mid-2026. Any proposal that treats him as a compute-cost or pipeline-throughput contributor is unsupported by attributable evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any attributable evidence from R0945 address genomic pipeline runtime, cloud instance cost, or workflow parallelisation rather than electronics quality-cost accounting?

findings.explanation: R1005 was ranked 4th on 'calling', 'batch', 'per sample', 'cost', 'hours'. His evidence is industrial microbiology/fermentation (Bacillus strain drift, metabolomics of broths, plasmid retention, seed-lot management) and only incidental short-read SNP calling for strain identity (E152/E089 at EUR 38 per isolate in 2017 prices), which is neither star-allele calling nor cloud cost optimisation of a Python/Snakemake pipeline. open_to (E070) and notes (E172) restrict him to fermentation/root-cause work and NTP companies with a fermentation step; he also reports limited availability (E172). He cannot be presented as addressing the 9 EUR/sample compute or 4-6h runtime problem.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is there any attributable R1005 evidence on reducing cloud compute cost or runtime for a clinical short-read allele-calling pipeline, as opposed to fermentation metabolomics?

findings.explanation: R0775 was ranked 5th because abstracts contain 'cutting', 'instances', 'per', 'cost', 'minutes'. All attributable content is 2D irregular nesting/cutting-plan optimisation for garment, textile and furniture manufacturing, plus a fabric-roll assignment patent (E068). Run-time and cost figures refer to nesting heuristics on polygon datasets, not to cloud compute for sequencing pipelines. open_to (E094) and notes (E047) restrict him to material-waste/nesting/CAD-CAM work with digitised pattern libraries, explicitly noting he is less suited to other kinds of projects. Material-yield savings do not transfer to the GenovaMed per-sample cloud bill.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any attributable R0775 evidence concern sequencing data processing, cloud VM cost, or bioinformatics workflow parallelism rather than textile nesting?

findings.explanation: R0751 was ranked 8th on 'price', 'pricing', 'serbian', 'consumers', 'cost'. His whole evidence set concerns hospitality/tourism revenue management, hotel reference-price experiments, GDPR-constrained personalised hotel rates, rate scraping and agritourism pricing. There is no bioinformatics, sequencing, cloud infrastructure, or pipeline performance content. Pricing of hotel rooms is not pricing of cloud compute or of pharmacogenomic tests, and his notes (E185) target property-management/revenue-management software and booking datasets, not diagnostics companies.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is there any attributable R0751 evidence on cloud compute cost, genomic pipeline throughput, or diagnostic test pricing under constrained reimbursement?

findings.explanation: R0595's spot/preemptible-instance work (E031/E144) is a stochastic bidding model with synthetic 30-day price series and 22% cost reduction versus a fixed-bid baseline; her remaining evidence is cost-sensitive classification, threshold selection, feature-selection stability and clinical tabular ML (E103, E083, E115, E041, E183, E044). This is modelling-side support for spot bidding and possibly for star-allele call decision thresholds, but there is no evidence of pipeline parallelisation, BWA/GATK-class alignment tuning, Snakemake optimisation, or hands-on sequencing-data engineering; her open_to (E159) is scoped to classification/LIS/model-evaluation consulting. Additionally she is on sabbatical in spring 2026 with availability limited to research collaboration and short consulting (E006), while the challenge needs an engineering optimisation effort. Counter-evidence: she should not be cited as a substitute for a pipeline/HPC engineer.
findings.recheckQuestion: Beyond E031's synthetic spot-market model, what attributable evidence shows R0595 has actually optimised the runtime or per-sample cloud cost of a real sequencing pipeline?

findings.explanation: R0633 was ranked 7th on 'price', 'pricing', 'current', 'instances', 'margin'. His evidence is workload-dependent/queueing-theoretic pricing for make-to-order metalworking and sheet-metal job shops, revenue management in ERP/MES environments and learning-curve cost models (E174, E128, E179, E008, E011, E017, E074, E075, E178). Some queueing/backlog-elasticity and cost-model ideas are conceptually adjacent to spot-instance bidding, but there is nothing on bioinformatics, spot markets as such, alignment/variant calling, or clinical accuracy preservation. His notes (E069) target NTP Novi Sad manufacturing/ERP/supply-chain companies. Treating him as a pipeline cost engineer would be unsupported.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any attributable R0633 evidence address cloud spot pricing or genomic data-processing pipelines, or only manufactured-job-shop pricing?

findings.explanation: R0781's only pipeline-throughput content is co-authorship (author position 1) on the GATK HaplotypeCaller scatter-gather/Snakemake study (E048); her first-authored work is Bayesian network structure learning on plant RNA-seq/proteomics (E165, E038, E055), scRNA reproducibility benchmarking (E099), and Serbian clinical relation extraction (E039). Her open_to (E175) is scoped to plant/agricultural omics and probabilistic graphical models, and her notes (E013) state she is less interested in applied software-development roles and offers an HPC cluster rather than cloud genomics experience. Counter-evidence: E048 demonstrates transferable WES throughput know-how (4.1h to 41min per sample with GIAB concordance), but her stated restrictions and non-genomics publication profile mean her expected engagement on a cost/throughput engineering task is weaker than a ranking based on shared-abstract matching implies. Also note the shared publication SYN-PUB-01614 is attributed to both R0123 (author 3, E082) and R0781 (author 1, E078) - it must not be counted twice as independent expertise.
findings.recheckQuestion: Will R0781 actually contribute to applied pipeline/speed engineering given her stated preference against applied software-development roles and her plant-omics open_to scope?

findings.explanation: Even for the strongest technical candidate R0123, the attributable evidence covers cloud spot cost modelling for WGS alignment/variant calling (E023/E177), a cloud/HPC orchestration layer project (E158), GATK scatter-gather throughput with Snakemake and GIAB concordance (E048), SV-breakpoint aligner benchmarking (E142), BAM soft-clip compression (E086) and cache-oblivious alignment layouts (E092). None of it addresses diplotype/star-allele (CYP2D6/CYP2C19) calling from targeted short-read panels, pharmacogene copy-number/phase resolution, ISO 15189 validation of a changed pipeline, or a <3 EUR per 24-sample-batch costing at GenovaMed's scale. Cost-optimisation magnitudes in the literature (41% spot reduction in stable periods, 18-34% penalty without checkpointing) also do not by themselves establish the 9 EUR to <3 EUR per sample target. Proposals must not claim clinical-accuracy preservation for star-allele calls on the basis of these records.
findings.recheckQuestion: What attributable evidence verifies any experience with star-allele/diplotype calling and its clinical validation, as distinct from generic variant calling or SV benchmarking?

findings.explanation: Complete restriction review: R0123 (E060/E088/E030) fits genomic-scale cost/throughput partnership and has one 2023 three-month audit with ~35% WES cloud-spend reduction - the only directly comparable prior engagement. R0781: plant/agricultural omics only, no formal industry employment (E090). R0945: electronics-only open_to, requires >=12 months defect/rework data, cannot accept broad academic-output IP assignment, capacity-limited until mid-2026 (E120). R1005: fermentation-only, limited availability H1 (E172). R0775: nesting/material-waste only, less suited to other project types (E047). R0595: classification/LIS scope, spring-2026 sabbatical, short engagements only (E006). R0633: manufacturing/ERP pricing scope; open to co-developing IP only where commercially promising (E069). R0751: hospitality tech/booking data, no engagements shorter than three months (E185). Where the Proposer's claims reference any candidate outside these stated scopes, the claim's participation premise is unverified.
findings.recheckQuestion: Which proposed engagements fall outside a candidate's stated open_to/notes scope or availability window, and how would that be reconciled?

findings.explanation: All content items were resolved to a candidate only via explicit author/inventor/participant bindings; no unattributedEvidenceIds exist in any of the eight bundles. However, each bundle carries multiple IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED diagnostics (other co-authors without internal researcher IDs), so the number of co-authors and co-author affiliations on these papers is only partially known, and the credited contribution of each candidate is fixed solely by author position (e.g. R0123 is often author 0 or 3; R0945 author 1-3; R1005 author 2). Author position alone does not establish that a candidate led the cost/throughput-relevant part of a paper. Conversely, no content was found that is attributed to a candidate without an identity binding.
findings.recheckQuestion: For each cited paper, does the candidate's author position and known role support the specific contribution being asserted, given unresolved co-author identities?

noCounterEvidenceFound: No unattributed content Evidence was found in any of the eight candidate bundles (unattributedEvidenceIds empty for R0123, R0781, R0945, R1005, R0775, R0595, R0633, R0751).
No identityFlags were raised on any of the eight candidates in the pool (identityFlags arrays empty).
No evidence was found that R0123's stated open_to/notes restrictions conflict with a genomic-scale cloud cost/throughput collaboration; his restrictions are compatible with the challenge.
No evidence was found of IP-assignment or data-access blockers for R0123; no such restriction appears in his registered profile evidence.

No counter-evidence was found showing that the specific runtime improvements reported in E048 (41 minutes per sample) or E023 (41% spot cost reduction in stable price periods) are invalid within their own stated experimental settings; the concern raised is transferability to star-allele panels and GenovaMed's scale, not internal validity.

No evidence was found in any bundle of prior work with pharmacogene (CYP2D6/CYP2C19) diplotype calling, so no candidate can be credited or discredited on that specific capability from registered evidence.
